system_commands.name: WRAP
system_commands.description: Pause the session without promoting anything. Writes the session summary to sessions.jsonl and overwrites last_session.json so the next boot has continuity — that's it. Does not touch task memory, does not run the verify/accept gate, does not write to semantic memory, does not rotate decisions.jsonl. Use this for 'taking a break' / 'stopping for now' — use MEMORY_CONSOLIDATE or TASK_CLOSE when the work is actually confirmed and ready to promote.

system_commands.name: MEMORY_CONSOLIDATE
system_commands.description: Deliberate promotion pass — invoke this when the work is actually confirmed and ready, not just when you're pausing (see WRAP for that). Extract rules from decisions/episodic logs to semantic memory (verify-before-promote, diff-before-delete, dedup — see core.memory.sk), then archive processed decisions.jsonl entries to decisions.archive.jsonl and sweep tasks/ for orphaned files whose branch no longer exists. On a feature/ticket branch, excludes the active task file entirely (untouched until TASK_CLOSE). On a protected branch (main/master/develop/release), the task file there is rolling working memory, not a ticket file — apply the same verify/accept gate as TASK_CLOSE to its contents, promote what qualifies, then clear it (don't archive it as if a ticket finished). Also writes the session summary to sessions.jsonl and overwrites last_session.json.

system_commands.name: TASK_CLOSE
system_commands.description: Full procedure in core.memory.sk. Resolves the task file for [branch] (default: current branch, sanitized per BOOT.md §2), verifies claims before promoting them to semantic memory, dedups against existing knowledge entries, then physically MOVEs the task file from .ai-os/memory/tasks/ to .ai-os/memory/archived_tasks/. Also writes the session summary to sessions.jsonl and last_session.json.

skill_commands.name: INFRA_MAP_DATAFLOW
skill_commands.description: Trace a data field forward to every place it's read/transformed/emitted (DB, outbound API, queue, file, cache, email), or trace backward from a sink to every input that can reach it -- for bug triage and change-impact analysis. A bare invocation with no field/sink/all is not a full-project scan -- it asks what to trace. Tool-gated (real dataflow tool if configured, else pattern-matching with per-finding confidence labels); does not write to semantic memory on its own, only on explicit confirmation via core.memory.sk's verify/accept gate

skill_commands.name: MEMORY_AMEND
skill_commands.description: Correct or retract an existing semantic-memory entry that turned out to be wrong or that caused a bug when followed -- the direction TASK_CLOSE/MEMORY_CONSOLIDATE don't cover, since they only add or supersede, never revisit an entry just because it was wrong. Verifies the claim is actually responsible, then corrects in place (stale fact), relocates to known_gotchas.md (true but harmful advice -- keep the lesson, not the recommendation), or removes outright (diff-before-delete). Same archetype-scaled accept gate as any other semantic-memory write

skill_commands.name: EVOLVE_BENCHMARK
skill_commands.description: On-demand only (never on boot -- would break BOOT.md SS2's cheap-by-design boot path). Compares this framework's actual current capabilities against leading AI agent frameworks/practices, writes genuine gaps as new PROPOSED evolution proposals in progress.md -- research only, never auto-applies. Tool-gated: WebSearch when available for current external claims, else flags findings as knowledge-cutoff-bounded rather than presented as verified fact (R21). Cross-checks progress.md's past proposals first so a gap already considered and deliberately rejected isn't re-proposed without new information (R8).
